title: Tidy Landmark Survival Analysis
text: Provides tidy framework landmark survival analysis, facilitating construction landmark-specific risk sets, incorporation longitudinal covariates, estimation associations time--event outcomes. Supports covariate estimation using last observation carried forward (LOCF) linear mixed-effects models (LME), alongside Cox proportional hazards Fine-Gray competing risks regression. Offers consistent reproducible workflow conducting analyses across multiple landmark times.

title: Construct landmark risk sets — landmark_data
text: data data frame one row per subject, holding follow-time, event status baseline predictors. id <tidy-select> subject identifier column. must unique non-missing. type preserved .id. time <tidy-select> Numeric, non-negative, finite time common origin (time zero) first event censoring. status <tidy-select> Event indicator. either: numeric: 0 censoring positive integers 1, 2, ... event types. Codes target cause treated competing events fit_landmark(). factor: first level censoring later levels event types. recoded 0, 1, 2, ... level order. mapping stored object's configuration. landmarks non-empty numeric vector unique, non-negative landmark times original time scale. Landmarks processed ascending order regardless input order. horizon NULL (default) follow-subject's observed time, single positive number giving follow-window relative landmark. example, horizon = 180 landmark 90 ends follow-original time 270.

title: Construct landmark risk sets — landmark_data
text: landmark_tbl, tibble subclass. leading columns : .id: subject identifier, original type. .landmark: landmark time original scale. .time: follow-since landmark. always strictly positive. .status: integer, 0 censored 1, 2, ... event type. .horizon: configured horizon, NA follow-unbounded. remaining baseline columns follow. Rows ordered landmark, original row order data. Use tibble::as_tibble() drop class metadata.

title: Construct landmark risk sets — landmark_data
text: Eligibility. subject risk set landmark \(s\) exactly \(T_i > s\). subject whose event censoring recorded \(s\) eligible. Time status. eligible subjects, .time \(T_i - s\) horizon NULL, \(\min(T_i - s, w)\) otherwise. .status keeps original code \(T_i - s \le w\), event exactly horizon retained. Otherwise .status becomes 0. Columns. original id, time status columns replaced reserved columns . columns carried unchanged, subjects never dropped missing baseline predictors. data already contains reserved column name, function throws error. landmark eligible subjects triggers warning. contributes zero rows still appears configuration printed counts.

title: Tidy a landmark dataset — tidy.landmark_tbl
code: subjects <- data.frame(   patient_id    = 1:10,   followup_days = c(20, 30, 48, 65, 85, 110, 145, 190, 250, 270),   event         = c(1, 2, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 0, 1) ) lm_dat <- landmark_data(   subjects, patient_id, followup_days, event,   landmarks = c(30, 60, 90), horizon = 180 ) tidy(lm_dat) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   landmark n_at_risk n_censored n_event_1 n_event_2 #>      <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>     <int> #> 1       30         8          3         3         2 #> 2       60         7          3         2         2 #> 3       90         5          1         3         1 tidy(lm_dat, show_proportion = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 3 × 6 #>   landmark prop_at_risk n_at_risk n_censored n_event_1 n_event_2 #>      <dbl>        <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>     <int> #> 1       30          0.8         8          3         3         2 #> 2       60          0.7         7          3         2         2 #> 3       90          0.5         5          1         3         1  # With a factor status, event columns can be named after its levels subjects$event <- factor(   subjects$event, levels = 0:2, labels = c("censored", "relapse", "death") ) lm_fac <- landmark_data(   subjects, patient_id, followup_days, event,   landmarks = c(30, 60, 90), horizon = 180 ) tidy(lm_fac, status_labels = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   landmark n_at_risk n_censored n_relapse n_death #>      <dbl>     <int>      <int>     <int>   <int> #> 1       30         8          3         3       2 #> 2       60         7          3         2       2 #> 3       90         5          1         3       1
